title: Adaptive cache-key shaping and staged surge-mitigation rollout for KV/prefix policies
creator: Aditi Rao
description:
Goal: Automate per-tenant cache-key shaping recommendations and a staged surge-mitigation rollout that safely applies TTL/policy changes while preserving latency SLOs and limiting token cost regressions. Problem: static per-prefix TTLs and naive keying cause either excessive cache churn (high cost) or stale hit-rates (high latency and token spend). This ticket implements a lightweight hit-rate model, a stochastic surge simulator, and an orchestrated staged-apply workflow with automatic rollback triggers.

Scope:
- Build an offline hit-rate estimator that ingests prefix request traces and outputs per-prefix hit-probability curves vs TTL.
- Implement a compact key-shaping heuristic that suggests merging/splitting of prefixes and optional affix trimming rules.
- Create a surge-mitigation simulator to predict worst-case KV lookup amplification during policy changes (shadow-run mode).
- Add staged apply operator: dry-run -> shadow-canary -> small-canary -> 25/50/100% rollout with health gates and cost/latency thresholds.
- Automatic rollback policy with hysteresis and a human-notify escalation path.

Success criteria / acceptance:
- Simulator predictions within ±15% of observed hit-rate/loss in canary experiments for 80% of tested prefixes.
- No canary that fails to meet latency or cost SLOs is promoted; all rollouts must be reversible within 10 minutes via automatic rollback.
- Average token cost reduction ≥6% for targeted tenants when recommendations applied, without >1% increase in P99 latency.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use a lightweight, explainable hit-rate model (exponential decay + heatmap smoothing) instead of a heavy ML model to keep runtime interpretable and fast to compute for many prefixes.
- Favor conservative prefix merges (only when high mutual affinity) to avoid over-broadening keys that might reduce hit-rate.
- Prefer staged rollout with short steady-state windows over an immediate aggressive apply; this reduces time-to-detect regressions at the cost of slower deployment.

Telemetry and metrics:
- Track per-prefix: requests/sec, observed-hit-rate, simulated-hit-rate, TTL, effective KV lookups per request, token cost delta.
- Rollout health gates: 5m rolling error increase, 1h rolling latency delta (p50/p95/p99), token cost per request.
- Anomaly detection: sudden drop in hit-rate >10% or spike in KV ops >25% triggers auto-rollback.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests: hit-rate estimator math, key-shaping heuristics, simulator stat properties.
- Integration: shadow-canary on staging using real production shadow traces for 72h.
- Chaos: inject synthetic prefix popularity bursts to validate rollback triggers and surge-mitigation behavior.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge feature flags and telemetry instrumentation behind ff:adaptive-cachekey (QA + canary).
2) Internal staging shadow-run for 72h and compare simulator vs observed.
3) Small external canary on 3 tenants with known workloads (low impact).
4) Progressive 25/50/100% with mandatory hold windows and auto-rollback gates.

Open questions:
- Should we include request fingerprinting (hashed context) to better separate similar prefixes, or will that increase key cardinality too much? (engineering + product to decide)
- Do legal/compliance teams require extra consent for storing prefix traces beyond current retention policy?
